newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Petaluma half yr profit rises 5.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Petaluma half yr profit rises 5.3 pct.

text.p: Winemaker Petaluma Ltd said on Tuesday its net profit for the half year to December 31 rose 5.3 percent to A$1.73 million from A$1.64 million a year ago.
Executive chairman Brian Croser said in a statement the result was in line with expectations.
The Petaluma group, which includes the Petaluma, Knappstein Wines and Mitchelton brands, was set to achieve its budget for 1996/97, he said.
However, Croser warned that despite strong first half growth in the domestic market, month-by-month trading remained patchy.
"I am still wary about the constrained household income growth and its eventual effect on premium wine sales, despite wine's apparent preferred position among retail goods," he said.
Croser said Petaluma's vineyards were set for a good quantity, high quality 1997 vintage despite an earlier frost problem in the Goulburn Valley in Victoria.
